quizzes.title: Background of Bilateral Ties: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage: India and Canada are working to reset their relationship. During a visit to India, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney signalled this reset, and cooperation between the two countries was described as widening across trade, energy and technology. The visit produced several outcomes in different sectors. Canada announced its intent to join the International Solar Alliance and was upgraded to full membership of the Global Biofuels Alliance. Both sides also signed a memorandum of understanding to build secure and resilient supply chains in critical minerals, an effort that aligns with the G7 Critical Minerals Action Plan. The minerals memorandum is one of the outcomes cited in the booklet. Canada will offer fully funded research internships to 300 Indian students each year. India remains the largest source of international students to Canada. The two countries also conduct joint research, which is part of the wider relationship. A technology and innovation partnership was launched to focus on emerging technologies, digital innovation and advanced manufacturing. In agriculture, a centre of excellence was established to work on fortified pulse products and food innovation. Many of these outcomes were announced during the same visit. Each outcome is linked to a specific sector, from solar energy to agriculture. Taken together, these outcomes cover energy, minerals, education, technology and agriculture.

questions.q: Which Indian agency collaborates with the Canadian Space Agency?
questions.explanation: The booklet names ISRO as the Indian partner in space collaboration with the Canadian Space Agency.

questions.q: Bilateral trade between India and Canada was worth how much in 2024?
questions.explanation: The booklet gives bilateral trade of USD 30.9 billion in 2024.

questions.q: In which year did Canada assist India in building the CIRUS nuclear research reactor?
questions.explanation: The booklet dates Canada's assistance with the CIRUS reactor to 1954.

questions.q:
Read the statements.
Assertion (A): The Nuclear Cooperation Agreement facilitates uranium supply and oversight.
Reason (R): The Nuclear Cooperation Agreement was dated 2013.
options: Both A and R are true and R explains A
Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are in the booklet, but the 2013 date does not explain the agreement's purpose.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Diplomatic ties established   ->   A. USD 30.9 billion
II. CIRUS reactor   ->   B. 2013
III. Nuclear Cooperation Agreement   ->   C. 1947
IV. Bilateral trade in 2024   ->   D. 1954
questions.explanation: Diplomatic ties date to 1947, the CIRUS reactor to 1954, the agreement to 2013, and the 2024 trade figure is USD 30.9 billion.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. ISRO collaborates with the Canadian Space Agency.
II. Canada assisted India in building the CIRUS reactor in 1954.
III. The Nuclear Cooperation Agreement is dated 2010.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement III is wrong because the booklet dates the Nuclear Cooperation Agreement to 2013.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
The Nuclear Cooperation Agreement facilitates uranium supply and oversight.
Diplomatic ties between India and Canada were established in 1957.
Bilateral trade was worth USD 30.9 billion in 2024.
ISRO collaborates with the Canadian Space Agency.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The 1957 statement is wrong because the booklet gives 1947, so three statements are correct.

quizzes.title: Khalistan Movement: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage: The Khalistan movement is rooted in Sikh identity, history and faith, and in politics around Punjab. Sikh identity is marked by the Khalsa tradition, which also stresses autonomy. Water sharing disputes between states fuelled tensions, and the Punjabi state demand was another part of the background. Several security operations were carried out against militancy in Punjab over the years. One operation focused on capturing militants from the outskirts of Punjab. The movement also has an international dimension. Diaspora-based separatists leveraged political influence in host countries, and some groups were organised to gain legitimacy and keep the issue alive. Pakistan's alleged support, including arms, funds and safe havens for militants, intensified hostilities. Periodic violence has been linked to Khalistani elements, and such elements have disrupted Indian diplomatic missions overseas. Indian counter-insurgency tactics have been criticised by global agencies, which has raised human rights concerns. Trade agreements have also been affected by political friction over the issue. Security and human rights concerns have both been part of the debate. The movement also has geopolitical implications, including concerns about India's sovereignty. Violent episodes have shaped the issue, and diaspora activism continues to affect bilateral ties. Continued radicalisation has been noted as a concern.

questions.q: The Khalsa tradition, which marks Sikh identity and autonomy, was established in which year?
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the Khalsa tradition to 1699.

questions.q: Which resolution demanded greater autonomy for Punjab?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Anandpur Sahib Resolution demanded greater autonomy for Punjab.

questions.q: Which operation removed militants from the Golden Temple?
questions.explanation: The booklet says Operation Black Thunder removed militants from the Golden Temple.

questions.q:
Read the statements.
Assertion (A): Operation Woodrose was a crackdown on Khalistani supporters across Punjab.
Reason (R): Operation Black Thunder removed militants from the Golden Temple.
options: Both A and R are true and R explains A
Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are in the booklet, but the Black Thunder fact does not explain the Woodrose crackdown.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Anandpur Sahib Resolution   ->   A. Crackdown on Khalistani supporters across Punjab
II. Operation Black Thunder   ->   B. Face of Sikh militancy advocating Khalistan
III. Operation Woodrose   ->   C. Demand for greater autonomy for Punjab
IV. Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale   ->   D. Removal of militants from the Golden Temple
questions.explanation: The Anandpur Sahib Resolution, Black Thunder, Woodrose and Bhindranwale match demands, removals, crackdowns and militancy roles in that order.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Khalsa tradition was established in 1699.
II. Indira Gandhi was killed by her Sikh bodyguards in 1984.
III. Khalistani groups found support only in Canada.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement III is wrong because the booklet lists support in Canada, the UK, the US and Australia.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
The Partition of India in 1947 left Sikhs as a minority.
The Anandpur Sahib Resolution demanded greater autonomy for Punjab.
Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale advocated Khalistan.
The Air India bombing was carried out by Sikh extremists based in the UK.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The Air India statement is wrong because the booklet says the Sikh extremists were Canada-based, so three statements are correct.

quizzes.title: Vienna Conventions and Diplomatic Immunity: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage: Relations between India and Canada have been tested by a series of disputes in recent years. The booklet presents these disputes as major challenges in the relationship. One of them followed the killing of a Khalistani leader, after which allegations were made about a possible link with Indian agents. The disputes also raised questions about the rules that govern diplomats and their missions. Two international agreements set the framework for diplomatic and consular relations between nations. These agreements cover the status of diplomats, the premises of diplomatic missions and the work of consular officers. The conventions describe the protections that diplomats and consular officers receive, and the booklet summarises them as key provisions. Diplomatic ties between the two countries have deteriorated in this period. Economic ties have also been affected, and the rifts have created uncertainty about Canadian investment in India. Students and applicants are among those affected by these challenges, according to the booklet. Visa and immigration matters form one of these challenges. The booklet also notes that the disputes have been linked to the wider geopolitical context. Against this background, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney signalled a reset with India during his visit, and the two sides moved to widen cooperation across trade, energy and technology.

questions.q: The Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations is dated to which year?
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations to 1961.

questions.q: Diplomats are protected from which of the following?
questions.explanation: The booklet says diplomats are protected from arrest and legal processes.

questions.q: Amid the diplomatic dispute, which step did both countries take?
options: Expelling diplomats and freezing consular services
questions.explanation: The booklet says both countries expelled diplomats and froze consular services.

questions.q:
Read the statements.
Assertion (A): Consular officers can perform their duties without interference.
Reason (R): Missions cannot be entered without permission.
options: Both A and R are true and R explains A
Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are in the booklet, but the rule on entering missions does not explain why consular officers work without interference.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Diplomatic immunity   ->   A. Missions cannot be entered without permission
II. Inviolability of diplomatic premises   ->   B. Consular officers can perform duties without interference
III. Protection of consular officers   ->   C. Protection from arrest and legal processes
IV. Vienna Convention on Consular Relations   ->   D. Dated 1963
questions.explanation: Diplomatic immunity covers protection from arrest, inviolability covers missions, consular protection covers duties without interference, and the consular convention is dated 1963.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations is dated 1961.
II. The Vienna Convention on Consular Relations is dated 1961.
III. Diplomatic immunity protects diplomats from arrest and legal processes.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because the booklet dates the Consular Relations convention to 1963.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Consular officers can perform duties without interference.
Missions can be entered without permission.
The Vienna Convention on Consular Relations is dated 1963.
The Vienna Convention on Consular Relations is dated 1961.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Only two statements are correct, because missions cannot be entered without permission and the consular convention is dated 1963.

questions.q: What term describes the protection that shields diplomats from arrest? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes diplomatic immunity as the protection that keeps diplomats from arrest and legal processes.

questions.q: What principle bars entry into diplomatic missions without permission? (one word)

questions.q: Besides expelling diplomats, what did both countries freeze in the dispute? (two words)
